title: Residential Clean Energy Credit (IRC 25D)
headline: The 30% Federal Solar Tax Credit Ended for 2026 Purchases
summary: Homeowners who researched solar in the past expect a 30% tax rebate to offset their purchase. Under Public Law 119-21 (OBBBA), Section 25D generally does not apply to expenditures made after December 31, 2025.

effective_dates.notes: Terminated for expenditures made after Dec 31, 2025 (installation completion date typically controls).

percent_or_amount: 0% for qualifying homeowner expenditures made after Dec 31, 2025.
homeowner_eligibility_notes: If you buy your own system with cash or a loan and installation is completed after December 31, 2025, you generally cannot claim the federal residential credit. The date installation is completed (placed-in-service timing under IRS rules) matters more than the contract date.
claim_howto: Not applicable for most 2026 installs. Prior-year eligible claims used IRS Form 5695. Carryforward rules for unused prior credits may still apply — consult a tax advisor. SolarFlow is not a tax advisor.

sections.heading: Why did the federal solar tax credit end?
sections.body: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA / Public Law 119-21), signed July 4, 2025, the Residential Clean Energy Credit (Section 25D) was terminated for expenditures made after December 31, 2025. The prior multi-year phase-down schedule does not apply to post-2025 expenditures. Confirm details on IRS FAQs for OBBB.

sections.heading: How solar leasing is pitched in 2026
sections.body: While residential 25D is gone for new homeowner purchases, commercial investment credit pathways (e.g., Section 48E for third-party-owned systems) may still appear in lease/PPA pricing — subject to their own deadlines and safe-harbor rules. Cash buyers should not assume a 30% federal rebate. Get ownership structure and credit assumptions in writing.

faqs.question: Can I claim the solar tax credit if I sign a contract in 2026?
faqs.answer: Generally no for a homeowner-owned cash or loan purchase if installation completes after Dec 31, 2025. Contract date alone does not save the credit. Confirm with a tax advisor.

faqs.question: Does SolarFlow still apply a 30% ITC to ROI?
faqs.answer: No. SolarFlow’s 2026 planning model treats federal residential ITC as 0% for homeowner-owned systems unless you explicitly model otherwise with an advisor.

common_myths: The credit steps down to 26% later this decade (False for typical 2026 residential purchases — 25D terminated for post-2025 expenditures).
Signing a contract in 2025 guarantees the credit even if install finishes in 2026 (Generally false — installation completion timing controls).

sources.title: IRS FAQs — OBBB modifications to 25C/25D and related credits
